Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Money, work & business

resources noun

means: money, property and supplies

also resource, means, funds, assets, wealth, riches, natural resources, asset

classical

Ov. Tr. 4.10.22: Maeonidēs nūllās ipse relīquit opēs
Cic. Tusc. 5.61: cōpiās ejus, opēs, majestātem dominātūs

opēs, opum f. pl.

noun, third declension, plural

resources, means, wealth

Means of every kind: money, property, power (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • dīvitiae, dīvitiārum f. pl. — riches, wealth

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 1320: dīvitiās tū quidem habuistī lūculentās; Cic. Att. 1.4.3: superō Crassum dīvitiīs, I am richer than Crassus; Traupman 157

    Riches as such, the opposite of poverty (see poverty); opēs are means and power as well.

  • facultātēs, facultātum f. pl. — means, what one can afford

    noun, third declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.42: nē major benignitās sit, quam facultātēs; Plin. Ep. 2.4.3: modicae facultātēs

  • cōpiae, cōpiārum f. pl. — resources, supplies; an army’s forces

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.61

Examples

  • saepe pater dīxit 'studium quid inūtile temptās? Maeonidēs nūllās ipse relīquit opēs'

    my father often said, ‘Why take up something so useless? Homer himself left no money’Ov. Tr. 4.10.21–22

  • Sunt quidem omnīnō nōbīs modicae facultātēs, dignitās sūmptuōsa

    My means, it is true, are modest, and my position is costlyPlin. Ep. 2.4.3

  • homō doctus in sē semper dīvitiās habet

    a learned man always has his riches within himselfPhaedr. 4.23.1

See also money, fund, supply, property, rich, poverty.
